subject: MSA/Order Form: downtime allocation & ops handshake
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@vertexsys.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: mark.h@vertexsys.com
Date: 2028-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA / Order Form — downtime allocations and credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. We reviewed the SLA sections with our ops and procurement teams. Two items are blockers for us:

1) Maintenance window: the proposed weekly 4-hour maintenance window during PST night is fine, but your MSA allows Redwood to schedule "emergency maintenance" outside that window with 6 hours' notice. We need smaller emergency windows (no >2 hours without explicit approval) and a firm cap on monthly out-of-window downtime.

2) Service credits: the table in the order form caps credits at 10% of monthly fees. For production workloads that power customer-facing features, our finance insists on a steeper credit curve for sub-99.5% availability and a clearer definition of how partial-day outages are measured (per-region vs global).

Attached is a short note from our SREs on how they measure availability. Can you point me to your suggested language or a counterproposal? We want to keep moving but procurement will not sign otherwise.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call today if easier.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships
Vertex Systems

Attachments: vertex_sre-availability-note.pdf (text summary)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@vertexsys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — downtime allocations and credits

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the SRE summary. Appreciate the specificity.

Quick thoughts:
- Emergency maintenance: we can tighten the language. Proposed internal compromise: 2-hour emergency window with 4-hour notice for non-critical infra items, and for true P0 safety/security events Redwood retains the right to act immediately but will provide post-action RCA and a pro-rated credit if the action causes customer-visible downtime beyond 30 minutes.
- Service credits: we can expand the credit curve for this deal tier. I propose we add a mid-tier credit at 99.0–99.5% and increase the top cap to 25% for sustained outages below 98.0%. We will also add a clause that availability is measured per-region unless you elect a global measurement at signing.

I'll loop in Laura (legal) and Priyom (sales ops) to put suggested redline language together and return a marked-up MSA + order form. If you're open, let's schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to triage and record any operational constraints.

— Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@vertexsys.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood MSA v3 — redlines on maintenance and credits (attached)

Elena — attaching a redlined MSA and an updated service-credit-matrix. Key changes we propose (summary):

- Emergency maintenance: replace open-ended language with a two-tier approach. Tier 1 (security/safety): immediate action allowed; Redwood provides RCA and a remedial credit if customer-visible downtime exceeds 30 min. Tier 2 (operational emergency): 4-hour notice and no more than 2 hours outside the standard maintenance window without prior approval.
- Measurement: default to per-region availability. We've included optional language you can tick for global measurement at signing.
- Credit matrix: added a 99.5–99.9 band with a modest credit and a steeper scale below 99.0 up to 25% cap for this enterprise order form.
- Measurement methodology: clarified that partial-day outages will be aggregated into incident windows; credits computed pro-rata to the impacted billing period.

We intentionally kept the security carve-out broad to preserve our ability to respond to zero-day threats — we can discuss narrower language if Vertex requires a prior notice obligation in all but the most urgent circumstances.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.pdf; service-credit-matrix.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@vertexsys.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: mark.h@vertexsys.com
Date: 2028-08-19T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA v3 — redlines on maintenance and credits (attached)

Laura / Rishi — thank you for the fast turnaround and for addressing most points. Two follow-ups from procurement and SRE:

1) Security carve-out: procurement asks for an obligation to provide notification "as soon as reasonably practicable" after any emergency action and a commitment to a post-action briefing within 72 hours. They will accept a narrow immediate-action carve-out for events that are certified by Redwood security as "critical vulnerability exploited in the wild."

2) Credit caps: Vertex is comfortable with the steeper curve but asks that the 25% cap be limited to multi-day incidents (more than 48 hours continuous degradation) and that there be a separate treatment for incidents caused by third-party cloud provider outages (explicitly excluded or subject to different credit rules).

If you can incorporate those two edits, we are ready to route to procurement for signature and to coordinate the DocuSign flow.

- Elena
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@vertexsys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-20T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA v3 — redlines on maintenance and credits (attached)

Elena — great, thanks. Action items and next steps:

1) Laura will: (a) add the "as soon as reasonably practicable" notice language for security carve-outs; (b) limit the 25% cap to incidents >48 hrs; (c) add explicit third-party cloud provider carve-out language with a separate credit schedule. Expect an updated redline by EOD Pacific today.
2) Priyom will: prepare an updated service-credit-matrix (xlsx) with the revised bands and include an example calculation for a 12-hour partial outage in a single region.
3) Rishi will: open the DocuSign envelope once legal confirms the final redline and send a calendar invite for a 30-min signoff sync (optional).

If that timeline works for Vertex, we'll aim to get signatures this week. Thanks for the quick collaboration — appreciate the detailed SRE notes, they made the tradeoffs easier to quantify.

— Rishi
